statusLine: M1 enemy flow built · awaiting your playtest · working on M2
facts: M0 done; M1 built, reviewed and committed (awaiting your playtest); M2 in progress
Tests, playable check, reviewer, your playtest

log.what: Your 24 requests received. Branch v5-live-game created from the V4 tip (f1b9a4cf).

Mapped the current game with three read-only searches (content and balance; menu, backend and web3; art) and two web research tasks (survivor-like balance; Solana, MagicBlock, wallets and multiplayer). Research saved in plan/v5/research/.
Independent reviewer agent written: .claude/agents/v5-reviewer.md (read-only; reviews the plan and each phase's code).
Baseline in the open Editor: EditMode 307/307, PlayMode 49/49, console clean.
Plan written: 26 phases in six stages, 14 proposed decisions, 20 questions for you.

Independent plan review: 3 blockers, 12 majors, 7 minors. All fixed in plan rev 2: a replay-verification spike before accounts, pending RUM until verified, no RUM-to-token bridge through items, anti-collusion rules, wager formats per mode, split phases (now 29, M0–M28). Details under Review findings.
GDD updated: three Decision log rows (V5 direction, reversals, two economies and custody), the roadmap's V5 track, the Not now and Never lists, and 27 V5 questions on the board.

Plan re-review of rev 2: no blockers, 5 majors and 6 minors (server-issued seeds, capped legacy RUM on migration, the fallback that would amend D6, two oversized phases, the real-time no-go path). All fixed in plan rev 3: M9b (conditional kinematic port), M10/M10b and M26/M26b splits, an early netcode measurement in M9.

Your answers to the V5 questions applied as plan rev 4: custody on our Railway server, a Monte Carlo balance simulator instead of autopilot runs, one enemy cap sized for a low-end phone, endless overtime, RUM treasury and vault, anti-collusion deferred, and more (decision D17). Researched and explained what you asked about: Photon and the other multiplayer options with costs, sign-in, hosting, Megabonk's levels, the four weapons plus eight more ideas, replay verification, and a cost breakdown of every third-party account (about $5–20 a month at 100 players). See Your answers, explained.

Independent review of your answers (rev 4): no blockers, 6 majors, 7 minors, all fixed in rev 5: custody safeguards (master-key backup and rotation, separate secrets, one-time key export), numeric pass limits for the Photon test in M9, the enemy cap set on your reference phone in M1, deferred anti-collusion switches still tested. Three new questions (Q31–Q33).

Your second round of answers applied as plan rev 7: 6 full-loot AI raids a day, uncapped PvP RUM, Google + email sign-in, Railway only, evolutions at level 8 with multi-level rare cards, nine new weapons (M4, M4b), a new Monte Carlo simulator written from scratch on V4 with ten player personalities, plausibility checks with value-moving modes played on our match server (moved up to M13b), no key export. Researched the 4-player Hunt netcode (recommendation now Fish-Net + Bayou: Photon calls its server mode "not recommended" for browsers) and the reference phone (Galaxy A15 / A16 4G at a steady 30 fps; browser memory near 256 MB is the big constraint).

Independent review of rev 7: no blockers, 8 majors, 10 minors, all fixed in rev 8: plausibility bounds from the balance model, a hard 256 MB mobile memory limit, a prediction-ready ship controller, server-session costs measured in M9 (Railway estimate ~$30–60/month once sessions run), the multi-ship lobby as its own phase (M21), fully specified personalities. Two new questions (Q34, Q35).

Your third round of answers applied as plan rev 9: Unity Netcode for GameObjects for multiplayer (free; we write nearby-enemy filtering and lag compensation), treasury protection (vault 80% / treasury 20%, 8 h shield, 10% daily loss cap, 72 h for new players), the reference phone (Galaxy A15 / A16 4G at 30 fps), forfeits pay nothing but a genuine short match does, checked voyage RUM usable on devnet. Every V5 question is now answered. Added a per-service Railway cost breakdown with savings (about $20–25/month if ~30 of 100 players play daily; $40–45 if all do; about $14–33 with the three biggest savings).
You chose: carry on while away, commit and push each phase that passes its tests and review, stand-in instead of the phone, Unity restarts allowed. M0 committed and pushed.

M1 enemy flow built (unattended): a minimum crowd per minute (ten 1-minute waves with a jagged floor), four telegraphed hordes (ring, line, pack) with a lull before each and edge markers, breathing room after arenas, the boss kill and hordes, a lower floor during the boss fight, XP that merges instead of being lost. Off under the v3-parity preset. Independent review: 3 blockers, 4 majors, 9 minors, all fixed. EditMode 331/331, PlayMode 50/50, playable check 0 game errors. Found: today's WebGL build needs a 344 MB heap and a 160 MB download, above the phone budget (moved to M7).

next: Playtest M1 (enemy flow): three runs with a weak, an average and a strong build; see the M1 box on this page for what to look for.
Get the reference phone (Galaxy A15 or A16 4G) before M7: M1 found today's build needs 344 MB of memory where the phone allows about 256 MB.
Accounts (list and costs in the answers): Railway by M9; a domain, a Google Cloud project and Resend by M10b; Helius by M11; Firebase by M19.
open: Earlier GDD questions (21 left) are still on the board; the raid entry fee (question 4) feeds M15 and the pass price (question 5) feeds M20.
done: V5 questions, round 3 (30 Sep): netcode, treasury protection, reference phone, forfeits and checked RUM decided; every V5 question answered.
V5 questions, round 2 (30 Sep): 16 more decided (D17), personalities defined, the Hunt netcode and reference phone researched.
V5 questions answered (30 Sep): 19 decided (D17), the rest explained on this page; the plan reviewed again (rev 5).
V5 M0 setup (29 Sep): branch, reviewer agent, plan and research, green baseline.

M0.title: Tests
M0.text: Baseline green: EditMode 307/307 and PlayMode 49/49 in Unity 6000.3.11f1; no compile errors.

M0.title: Reviewer
M0.text: Agent file in place; it ran the plan review (below). In this session it runs through a general agent loading the same file; new sessions list it as v5-reviewer.

M0.title: Plan reviews
M0.text: Two independent reviews: rev 1 had 3 blockers, 12 majors, 7 minors; rev 2 had no blockers, 5 majors, 6 minors. All addressed in rev 3.

M1.title: What changed
M1.text: Ten 1-minute waves keep a minimum crowd alive (topped up one enemy every 0.35 s), four hordes (1:45 ring, 5:30 line, 7:40 pack, 9:15 ring) with a 10 s lull and edge markers, breathing room after big moments, XP merging. Data in the Saltwind timeline; the v3-parity preset turns it off.

M1.title: Tests
M1.text: EditMode 331/331 (24 new), PlayMode 50/50 (1 new: the crowd reaches each minute's floor in the real scene). Playable check with screenshots at 1, 3, 5:30, 6, 9 and 13 minutes: 0 game errors.

M1.title: Review
M1.text: 3 blockers (spawn gap, missing edge markers, stale evidence), 4 majors, 9 minors: all fixed. Table on this page under Review findings.

M1.title: Your playtest
M1.text: Play three runs (a weak, an average and a strong build). Does the crowd feel constant but changing minute to minute? Do the hordes (1:45, 5:30, 7:40, 9:15) read, with the arrow at the screen edge? Is there breathing room after the Reef Crab, the elites and the boss? F1 → Wave Timeline shows the flow line.

reviews.title: Plan review, rev 1 → rev 2 (29 Sep)
reviews.summary: The independent reviewer read the plan against your 24 requests, the research, the handoff rules, the GDD's never list and the current code. It found 3 blockers, 12 majors and 7 minors, and confirmed that the plan's claims about the existing code were accurate. All 22 are addressed in rev 2 (now 29 phases, M0–M28). A second review checks the fixes.

rows.finding: Server RUM trusted a client-uploaded run summary before any verification existed, against D6 and the handoff's rule on client-trust fallbacks.
rows.fix: Run RUM is now pending until verified and cannot be spent, transferred or wagered (D6, I10b.4).

rows.finding: Replay verification was assumed, not proven: unseeded draws (PickupModule, WorldPort), Rigidbody physics, no cost measured.
rows.fix: New M9 replay verification spike before accounts: seeding fixes, WebGL vs headless agreement over 10 runs, CPU per minute, go/no-go with named fallbacks (Q29).

rows.finding: RUM-bought items could be minted and sold for tokens: an indirect RUM-to-token bridge.
rows.fix: D4 now tracks item origin: anything bought, earned or traded with RUM stays web2 forever; island sales return RUM-bought parts to the seller (Q24).

rows.finding: The list of reversals missed token winnings (play-to-earn), token balances and the Arena draft.
rows.fix: D8 names all six reversals; Q26 asks you to confirm them.

rows.finding: NFT migration was planned before NFTs exist; royalty allow-lists block transfers by unlisted programs.
rows.fix: M13 migrates tokens, records and inventory; NFT migration moves to M26 through the game program.

rows.finding: No ownership sync for NFTs sold elsewhere; devnet external markets unconfirmed.
rows.fix: M26 adds an indexer or webhook with a reconcile job, and an honest devnet exit criterion (Tensor's open program).

rows.finding: No anti-collusion policy.
rows.fix: New D15 (linked accounts blocked, price bands, daily caps, review flags) wired into M15, M24, M26, M27; defaults in Q27.

rows.finding: Race and Hunt wager formats were undefined.
rows.fix: M24 defines Arena, Hunt and Race formats: entry windows, minimum entrants, refunds, unverified finishes.

rows.finding: A web3 playtest bought a decoration before decorations exist; phone measurement before the mobile build; an unrealistic hackathon option.
rows.fix: Playtest buys a store item; the cap is measured on desktop in M1 and on a phone in M7; Q1 option B rewritten.

rows.finding: The planned brain reused DevTools autopilots that never ship.
rows.fix: M16 rewrites the brain in Runtime with a test that Runtime never references DevTools (D10).

rows.finding: Player schedules stored as the designer-owned timeline asset (read as a singleton, hashed).
rows.fix: A schedule DTO in the base snapshot becomes an in-memory overlay at raid start; its hash enters raid records.

rows.finding: M1 and the old netcode-plus-Arena phase were too big for one gate.
rows.fix: Split: M1 enemy flow and M2 balance model; M21 netcode spike and M22 Arena.

rows.finding: Several phases lacked a playtest line or an automated check.
rows.fix: Every phase now has both (or an owner check for document and spike phases).

rows.finding: The .NET 8 target ends support on 10 Nov 2026.
rows.fix: The server moves to .NET 10 LTS in M10.

rows.finding: Raid loot currency undefined.
rows.fix: New question Q23 (suggested: RUM, split into an exposed treasury and a safe vault).

rows.finding: Wrong question numbers in two tasks.
rows.fix: Fixed in rev 2.

rows.finding: Siren Bell was said to charm; Grapeshot is an item, not a weapon.
rows.fix: Siren Bell slows and stuns; Grapeshot removed from the weapon options.

rows.finding: Onchain record rent and scope undefined.
rows.fix: Only value-bearing results are recorded; ordinary runs batch into the player record; match accounts close after settlement.

rows.finding: Web push needs a Firebase account, against the local-only rule.
rows.fix: D11 now covers third-party accounts; Q30 asks when to create them.

rows.finding: The v3-parity preset's status was unclear.
rows.fix: D16: it stays as a regression baseline until M28; new mechanics switch off under it.

rows.finding: Privy's server-held custody flow was unclear.
rows.fix: Q3 and M10/M11 spell out Privy server wallets with a server-verified token.

rows.finding: 'Saltwind only' narrowed the global kill board.
rows.fix: Option A is now every voyage biome as it ships.

reviews.title: Plan re-review, rev 2 → rev 3 (30 Sep)
reviews.summary: The reviewer re-checked rev 2: no blockers. 17 of the first 22 findings were fully resolved and 5 partly; it found 5 new majors and 6 minors, mostly about value integrity (seeds, migrated RUM, fallbacks) and phase size. All are addressed in rev 3 (31 phases plus the conditional M9b).

rows.finding: Fallback B (statistical checks) would pay RUM without a verified replay, and async modes would then need the later match server.
rows.fix: Choosing B now explicitly amends D6 and moves Stage E ahead of Stage C; fallback A got its own conditional phase M9b kinematic port.

rows.finding: The client picks the run seed, so a verified run could still be a rerolled easy seed.
rows.fix: Every value-earning run uses a server-issued seed that verification checks (D6, I10.2, M18).

rows.finding: Migration copied the editable local RUM balance into the server account.
rows.fix: Local RUM becomes capped legacy RUM: store-only, never transferred, wagered or exposed to raids (I10b.3).

rows.finding: The server phase and the marketplace phase were too big for one gate.
rows.fix: Split into M10 server and ledger / M10b accounts and migration, and M26 NFTs and ownership sync / M26b marketplace.

rows.finding: Stale references (the V4 save guard, art-guide updates, invites, question tags, D14 vs Q15, Q1 wording, assembly direction).
rows.fix: All corrected; art-guide update tasks added to M14, M25 and M27; invite tasks added to M22–M24.

rows.finding: The list of unseeded draws was out of date; the placeholder verifier project was not mentioned; client and server are two builds.
rows.fix: Corrected list; M10 replaces the placeholder with a verifier worker; both build ids are recorded.

rows.finding: Self-contradicting playtest wording.
rows.fix: Against a second tester's account.

rows.finding: Race base owners could wager on their own base; referrals were not covered.
rows.fix: Both covered by D15.

rows.finding: Brand bounty events depended on a later phase.
rows.fix: Marked as wired in M27.

rows.finding: Determinism was proved once and never re-checked.
rows.fix: A standing replay-determinism test joins gate step 6 from M10 on.

rows.finding: Six mechanics in one phase.
rows.fix: Accepted; watched when M1 is detailed.

rows.finding: The netcode spike had no no-go path, no multi-ship runtime task, and its risk was measured last.
rows.fix: No-go path (Arena with light PvE, Hunt reduced or dropped), a multi-ship runtime task, and an early bandwidth measurement in M9 (I9.5).

rows.finding: Siren Bell's stun was not in the design doc.
rows.fix: Now a damaging pulse with a 20% slow, per the design.

reviews.title: Review of your answers, rev 4 → rev 5 (30 Sep)
reviews.summary: The reviewer checked that every answer is reflected in the plan and that the explanations are accurate and plain. No blockers, 6 majors and 7 minors, all addressed in rev 5. It raised three new questions for you (Q31 reference phone, Q32 key export, Q33 master-key backup).

rows.finding: Overtime tiers and a run-ending pursuer were still mentioned after you chose the endless ramp.
rows.fix: Removed; M1 and M2 keep the endless ramp (Q22).

rows.finding: Keys on Railway: the master key and the database share one Railway project; no backup or rotation; fee payer and settle keys not separated.
rows.fix: D7 and a new risk row: offline master-key backup (Q33), a key id for rotation, separate secrets for the fee payer, treasury and settle authority.

rows.finding: Key export contradicted "keys never reach the client".
rows.fix: One-time export after a fresh sign-in, logged; the account then becomes self-custody (Q32).

rows.finding: Photon's docs call client-server modes on WebGL "not recommended"; the free plan caps relayed traffic at 0.3 TB a month.
rows.fix: New risk row; M9's test has numeric pass limits (≤ 60 ms added latency, ≤ 30 KB/s per player, ≤ 150 MB per 4-player match); Fish-Net + Bayou fallback; ANSWERS corrected.

rows.finding: One cap sized for a low-end phone was set only in M7, after M1–M3 tuning; no reference phone or frame rate.
rows.fix: The cap is set in M1 on your reference phone (new Q31); targets are shares of the cap; Hunt clients see at most the cap.

rows.finding: Referrals were still blocked though D15 turns limits off; AI raids, prizes and referrals missing from the risk; off-switches untested.
rows.fix: Hooks off (D15), each tested with its switch on; risk row lists every value flow.

rows.finding: Photon is needed for the M9 test, not only M21.
rows.fix: ANSWERS and TODOs say Photon from M9.

rows.finding: Leaderboard scope adopted before Q16 is answered.
rows.fix: Marked proposed.

rows.finding: "Cheating stays impossible" overclaimed; option B's stage-order effect missing.
rows.fix: "A changed result is always caught"; bots need separate checks; B moves the real-time stage earlier.

rows.finding: Tests still listed moderation states.
rows.fix: A stored report flag only on devnet.

rows.finding: Treasury and vault RUM on a plot sale unspecified.
rows.fix: They stay with the seller.

rows.finding: Dangling Q4/Q8/Q14 note; D17 missed Q3, Q18, Q23 and was out of order.
rows.fix: Inlined; D17 completed and reordered.

rows.finding: Megabonk claim stated as fact; the Balance Lab's editor window no longer exists.
rows.fix: Qualified as an estimate; M2 gives the lab a front end in the Tuning Console.

reviews.title: Review of rev 7 (30 Sep)
reviews.summary: Checked your second round of answers against the plan. No blockers, 8 majors and 10 minors, all addressed in rev 8 (33 phases). Two new questions for you: Q34 (forfeits) and Q35 (when checked voyage RUM can be wagered or sold).

rows.finding: "Kills can't exceed spawns" is weak: the game spawns more as you kill more.
rows.fix: Bounds now come from the balance model and simulator; tested against a forged but consistent 99th-percentile log.

rows.finding: Plausibility-checked RUM can still reach other players through wagers, the market and raids.
rows.fix: Stated in D6 and the risks; new question Q35.

rows.finding: With uncapped PvP RUM (Q10) and collusion checks off, instant forfeits mint RUM.
rows.fix: Suggested rule: forfeits and matches under a minimum length pay nothing (Q34).

rows.finding: "Heap near 256 MB, max 512" would crash 32-bit Chrome on the reference phone.
rows.fix: Hard 256 MB limit for mobile browsers (budget ~200 MB); 512 only on 64-bit browsers.

rows.finding: Too big for one gate.
rows.fix: Split: M13b single-player server sessions; new M21 multi-ship runtime and lobby before the Arena.

rows.finding: Client prediction needs a deterministic ship controller; the physics ship had no task.
rows.fix: M13b adds a prediction-ready ship controller; M9 tests responsiveness at 150 ms.

rows.finding: No measure of session cost, sessions per process or mobile latency.
rows.fix: M9 go-limits added; AI raids run headless faster than real time; Railway cost estimate (~$30–60/month) before M13b closes.

rows.finding: Parameters incomplete and values outside the declared enums.
rows.fix: Every personality has all 12 parameters with defined enums; avoidable damage and boss timing defined.

rows.finding: D11 timing, D4 AI-raid wording, a stale tag, floor-phone and 95% frame checks, assembly direction, invite order, request map rows, Quantum re-plan note, stale page cards, task order and profile mapping.
rows.fix: All corrected.

reviews.title: Review of rev 9 (30 Sep)
reviews.summary: Checked your third round: the Netcode for GameObjects choice, the forfeit rule and the Railway arithmetic (all within 20% of a recomputation). No blockers, 2 majors, 4 minors, all addressed.

rows.finding: Read before the round-3 update landed (Fish-Net Pro, open questions).
rows.fix: Already current; confirmed.

rows.finding: "Ranked only on request" was already in the baseline, so it double-counted.
rows.fix: Removed; reduced totals restated: ~$26–33 busy, ~$14–20 quiet.

rows.finding: Winner's pay on a forfeit, idle players, PvE sinkings and the Hunt's version were undefined.
rows.fix: One rule for both modes, with tests: nobody paid if others leave within 60 s; after that the remaining player is paid; 30 s idle counts as leaving; PvE, storm and edge wall count as combat.

rows.finding: Stale Quantum and "still open" text; Serverless listed as an extra saving.
rows.fix: Reworded; Serverless marked as already assumed, wake-up time measured in M9.

reviews.title: M1 enemy flow: implementation review (30 Sep)
reviews.summary: The reviewer checked the diff against the plan, the V4 rules and the evidence. 3 blockers, 4 majors, 9 minors; all fixed or recorded.

rows.finding: The PlayMode results predated the new M1 PlayMode test.
rows.fix: Both suites re-run after the last change; the test is in the evidence.

rows.finding: Several enemies could spawn in one frame, ignoring the 0.35 s spawn gap.
rows.fix: One top-up per gap; a flow-on gap test.

rows.finding: The planned edge markers were missing.
rows.fix: Horde warnings carry a direction; the HUD shows the edge arrow and a minimap ping.

rows.finding: Late hordes found no room at the enemy cap but still counted.
rows.fix: A 10 s lull before each horde, headroom above the cap, counted only when something spawns.

rows.finding: Members could be skipped on screen or placed without bounds checks.
rows.fix: Formed just beyond the view; islands and bounds always checked.

rows.finding: The phone deferral was not recorded.
rows.fix: Recorded in the plan (M1, M7) and your TODOs, with the memory finding.

rows.finding: Merging applied to all pickups; merged views kept old values.
rows.fix: XP only; the view is re-drawn.

rows.finding: Dead code, untested holds and releases, adaptive lever, version tag, stale status, text, a weak cap test, warning timing, a tool error, a magenta effect.
rows.fix: Fixed, or recorded as pre-existing (the magenta flame effect is V4's known placeholder).
